description: Given a company's domain and the sender address of an email that claims to be from it, say whether the address is on the company's own domain or a subdomain of it, a lookalike made to pass as it (look-alike characters, another ending, a typo, an extra word, or the name in front of someone else's domain), a free mail account or an unrelated domain. For the company's own domain, also reads the DMARC policy that applies to that exact address and its mail records, and says whether a forged copy would be refused, sent to spam or not blocked; for any other domain, when it was registered and whether it can send and receive mail. Flags a display name that claims the company or is itself an address. Use it when the user asks whether an email from a brand, bank or supplier is legit. The address alone never proves the content is safe; for one specific message, analyze_email_headers or verify_email_signature give stronger evidence.

brand.description: The real company's domain, e.g. example.com.

from.description: The sender as the mail app shows it, e.g. "Example Billing" <billing@mail.example.com>, or just its domain. Include the display name: a name that claims the company or is itself an address is flagged.

name: check_email_sender
title: Is this email really from them?
